name: Name
body: The Black Tide campaign follows the return of the Orgoth to the shores of the Iron Kingdoms for the first time in 400 years. This second season sees the invaders firmly entrenched in their assault, advanced to the great cities of the Iron Kingdoms but ground to a stalemate by the grit and will of the defending armies. The impasse will be short-lived, however, as strange circumstances make for strange allies, and new forces join the struggle for the future of the Iron Kingdoms!

name: Name
body:
Black Tide is an ongoing campaign for two or more players. The campaign takes place over four seasons with each season comprised of three chapters, delivered one chapter per month via subscription to the WARMACHINE app. Each chapter is comprised of three scenarios.
When playing the Black Tide campaign, each player chooses to play as either an Invader or a Defender. If players select the same allegiance, it will be necessary for players to play games as the opposing allegiance in order to facilitate all players having the opportunity to play through the three scenarios according to their chosen allegiance. Players should divide themselves between Invaders and Defenders as evenly as possible.
Scenarios are intended to be played in order but can be repeated for campaign groups of more than two players in order to allow all players to play each scenario in the role of their chosen allegiance. It is not necessary for all players to play each other, only that all players have the opportunity to play each scenario. Players should only gain War Chest points (see below) from their best result of a specific scenario each season. So, if a player repeats a scenario, only record the results of the highest score for that scenario; do not record the points from a specific scenario more than once.

name: Name
body: Character warjacks cannot be used in this campaign through normal army construction. Instead, they are created progressively by upgrading a preset warjack through with War Chest points (see below).

name: Name
body: Over the course of the Black Tide campaign, players will receive and track War Chest points to determine their success in the campaign. War Chest points are gained based on the outcome of scenario battles described at the end of each scenario. Beginning in Season Two, War Chest points may be spent between matches on a variety of benefits. Each player will be responsible for keeping a ledger of their own War Chest points. Be sure to add any War Chest points gained during a match to your total after the match and take care to accurately subtract the appropriate War Chest points from your total when you spend them for any benefits. A printable War Chest tracking sheet can be downloaded at Black Tide Season 2 War Chest Record Sheet

name: Name
body: There are three ways to spend your War Chest points during the course of the campaign: Strategic Advantages, Campaign Command Cards, and Character Warjack Upgrades.

name: Name
body:
Players can spend up to 4 War Chest points before a match for Strategic Advantages that provide a benefit during the course of the match. A Strategic Advantage is only good for the match you buy it for and does not carry over into subsequent matches.
Some Strategic Advantages can only be taken by the Underdog in match. The Underdog is the player who has the fewest War Chest points going into the match. If players are tied with War Chest points, there is no Underdog.
Normal Strategic Advantages cost 2 War Chest points. Underdog Advantages cost 1 War Chest point. Strategic Advantages can be added to your force list after Creating a Match in the WARMACHINE app by tapping the ADVANTAGES button at the bottom of the card list.

name: Name
body:
Campaign Command Cards are Command Cards designed specifically for use in the Black Tide campaign and are not meant for play in non-campaign games. Campaign Command Cards must be unlocked for use by paying 3 War Chest points. Once unlocked, they can be used in any subsequent game. Note that some Campaign Command Cards also have army point costs like other Command Cards.
Be sure to record any Campaign Command Cards you unlock so you know what is available to your force in later matches.
Campaign Command Cards will appear in your normal Command Card list in the WARMACHINE app and can be identified by the presence of "[CAMPAIGN]" in the title of the card.

name: Name
body:
In the Black Tide campaign, players using MKIV armies can use War Chest points to upgrade character warjacks. Character warjacks start with a stock loadout and can be upgraded over time by spending War Chest points. Each upgrade costs 3 War Chest points, and once an upgrade is purchased, it is a permanent change to the warjack for all subsequent matches. The benefit to upgrading a character warjack in this fashion is that the upgrades do not change the army point cost of the warjack, so as you upgrade it, the warjack gets a more valuable loadout, which is then permanently available to your force at a bargain cost.
When upgrading a character warjack, both arm weapons must be upgraded before the head can be upgraded. And the head must be upgraded before a bond can be selected. Once an upgrade is purchased, including a bond, it cannot be changed for the duration of the campaign.
Be sure to record your character warjack upgrades when you spend your War Chest points on them.

name: Name
body: When setting up to play Black Tide scenarios, players will take turns placing terrain on the table as described by the scenario. When placing terrain features, a player cannot place an obstacle or obstruction within 5" of another obstacle or obstruction.

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective uncontested.

name: Name
body: Scenario victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set number of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body:
Some Black Tide scenarios are designated as key battles. These are particularly large or important battles to the narrative of the campaign. Key Battle scenarios are noted in the title of the scenario. A player who wins a Key Battle scenario gains an additional War Chest point.
Players who are participating in the Resurrection League may choose to include the league model, Reinholdt, Gobber Spy, as part of their force. If they do, they may undertake a Gobber Spy mission during the Key Battles of this campaign to earn additional Victory Points. Gobber Spy missions are detailed in the Key Battle scenarios.

name: Name
body: In the war-torn lands of the Iron Kingdoms, in the relentless grip of what seemed like endless winter, Horruskh, the Thousand Wraths, the most fearsome warlord of the Orgoth Sea Raiders, regarded his legions with pride. Their ruthless invasion had left western Immoren embroiled in chaos and on its knees. And now, on the edge of their retreating frontlines, where the frigid winds whipping across the bitter battlefield could not blow the stench of death away, Cygnaran soldiers hunkered in their trenches, preparing for one final stand against their would-be conquerors. Despite the grim fate that would soon befall them, they sang. Tomorrow was Giving Day in the Iron Kingdoms, a moment of respite and hope when people exchanged gifts and well-wishes for the year to come. Horruskh, with his heart as cold as the icy rime that covered the land, despised the merriment of the Cygnarans. And yet these soldiers, beleaguered by war, stood united in their resolve, singing hymns of unity and bravery in the face of imminent destruction.

name: Name
body: It was the eve of what would be a momentous and bloody battle, but Horruskh, from his mountainside perch, observed the Cygnaran trenches with disdain. His hatred for their camaraderie and strength filled his heart with rancor. "Their joy is meaningless," he muttered, his voice a spiteful growl in the chilling air. Determined to extinguish the soldiers’ hope, Horruskh devised a wicked plan. He summoned an elite band of raiders, and under the cloak of night, they crept into the trenches, stealing the Cygnarans’ gifts, rations, and any token of misplaced hope, leaving behind nothing but a haunting silence. Returned to his camp, Horruskh basked in the afterglow of his villainous deeds as he waited restlessly for the rising sun that would call his army to battle. He relished the thought of breaking their spirits before breaking their bones, and he imagined the expressions of anguish he would be met with as the Cygnarans gasped their final breaths cowering in his shadow.

name: Name
body: But morning came, and as Horruskh readied his warriors, he heard something unexpected—the faint sound of singing. The Cygnaran soldiers, despite their loss and dire situation, sang songs of hope and courage, their voices rising above the howling winds. Baffled by their resilience, Horruskh paused. The soldiers’ unity and spirit perplexed him. He realized then that their strength lay not in material possessions but in their unbreakable bonds and unwavering resolve. In that moment, something within Horruskh stirred. A tiny spark of understanding flickered in his dark heart. Perhaps, just perhaps, unity was a power he had underestimated. And he vowed to exterminate it if it should take him a thousand lifetimes more. (With apologies to Theodore Geisel) Black Tide Season 4, Chapter 1 is made up of three scenarios that should be played in order: "Dark Celebration," "Nightfall," and "Full Assault."

name: Name
body: Amidst the joyous echoes of soldiers celebrating Giving Day, the atmosphere ruptures with sudden violence. In a calculated and malevolent move, the invaders descend upon the defenders' entrenched position. War cries drown out the festive tunes as the invaders, their dark war machines thundering, surge forward. Their intent is clear: to exploit the moment of celebration, creating maximum confusion and disarray as they clash with the defenders in a ruthless bid to conquer the battlefield.

name: Name
body:
Eager to break through the stalemate on the front lines that have bogged down in bitter trench warfare, the Invaders strike the Defenders at the height of their winter revelries. The Invaders’ plan is simply to take the Defenders by surprise in the midst of their celebrations in an attempt to overwhelm them before the Invaders can be repelled.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body:
The Defender builds a 50-point army.
The Invader builds a 75-point army.

name: Name
body:
The Invader deploys in an area 10" forward of the south table edge.
The Defender deploys in an area anywhere completely within 5" of a command trench.
As shown on the map, place one command trench lengthwise in the middle of the Defender Camp touching the north table edge. Place a second command trench abutting it toward the west table edge. Place a third command trench lengthwise touching the east table edge, 12" forward from the north table edge.
The Defender then places 5 additional trenches anywhere within the area of the Defender Camp.
Taking turns, each player then places three additional non-Trench terrain features. Terrain features can be placed anywhere within the area of No Man’s Land or the Defender Camp. A terrain feature cannot be placed within 4" of another terrain feature, including a trench.
The Invader cannot place Defenses when playing this scenario.
The Defender deploys first, and the Invader takes the first turn.

name: Name
body:
No Man’s Land: The entire area of No Man’s Land is considered rough terrain.
Reinforcements: For each command trench they hold, the Defender can return d3 small-based destroyed Grunts to play to one friendly unit within 2" of the held command trench.
Models return with 1 unmarked damage box. Place the returned Grunts within 2" of another model in their unit. Returned Grunts must forfeit their Normal Movement and Combat Actions the turn they are returned to play.

name: Name
body:
Starting with the Defender’s second turn, the Defender scores 1 Victory Point at the start of each of their turns for holding either a command trench or No Man’s Land.
Starting with the Invader’s third turn, the Invader scores 1 Victory Point at the start of each of their turns for each command trench they are holding.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If the Invader holds all three command trenches at any time, they win the match and receive 5 War Chest points. If the Invader has not won by the end of their sixth turn, the Defender wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only Leader model in play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader model in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: With hearts heavy but their resolve unyielding in the wake of devastation, the shattered defenders courageously commit to entering the treacherous no-man’s-land between their trenches and those of their enemies. Despite grievous losses at the hands of the invaders, their current mission remains clear: to recover the bodies of their fallen comrades. For these brave souls, retrieving their brothers-in-arms is a solemn duty that transcends the ongoing peril of death—an act of reverence and respect for those who valiantly fought beside them, a sacrifice they refuse to let fade into the cold embrace of the war-torn landscape.

name: Name
body:
Following a disastrous Defenders’ route after an assault on the Invaders’ frontlines, wounded soldiers dot the No Man’s Land between the forward trenches. The Defenders must recover their injured before they are captured by the enemy for interrogation or worse. With night falling and the ground growing cold, things are bound to go from bad to worse.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: Each player builds a 75- or 100-point army.

name: Name
body:
The Defender deploys in an area 10" forward of the north table edge.
The Invader deploys in an area 10" forward of the south table edge.
As shown on the map, center a command tent in the middle of each player’s Deployment Zone, abutting the rear table edge of their zone.
Then place three 30 mm prisoner objectives along the middle of the table, with the first in the center of the table, the second 8" from the west table edge, and the third 8" from the east table edge.
Taking turns, each player then places four additional trenches in their Deployment Zones.
Taking turns, each player then places three additional terrain features anywhere in No Man's Land.A terrain feature cannot be placed within 4" of another terrain feature or a prisoner objective.
The Defender deploys first and takes the first turn.

name: Name
body:
Nightfall: While playing this scenario, all models gain concealment.
No Man’s Land: The entire area of No Man’s Land is rough terrain.
Prisoners: A warrior model within 1" of an unsecured prisoner objective can make a special action to secure the objective. Place the prisoner objective in base contact with the securing model. When the securing model is moved or placed, its controller places the prisoner objective anywhere in base contact with that model. An independent warrior model securing a prisoner objective suffers –2 SPD. A unit securing a prisoner objective suffers –1 SPD.
A friendly warrior model within 1" of a prisoner objective secured by another friendly model can make a special action to take control of a prisoner objective. That model is now considered to be the securing model. Place the prisoner objective in base contact with the new securing model. A friendly model can take control of a prisoner objective only if that objective has not already been placed this turn.
If the model securing a prisoner objective is destroyed or removed from play, the objective is no longer considered secured.

name: Name
body:
A player scores 1 Victory Point at the start of their turn for each prisoner objective they are securing.
A player scores 2 additional Victory Points the first time each prisoner objective is placed within the area of their command trench.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If a player starts their turn holding their opponent’s command trench, they win the match and receive 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only Leader model in play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader model in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: As the invaders press their advantage, time is running out for the defenders. With the onset of spring muddying the wintry landscape, desperation fuels a final gambit to halt the invaders’ advance. In a race against time, they work to expand their trench network, their hopes hanging on the belief that they might exploit a perceived weakness in the invaders' own fortifications. With shovels and determination, they toil frantically, their efforts a heroic bid to turn the tide of battle before the invaders seize a definitive victory.

name: Name
body:
With the spring thaw, it becomes increasingly apparent that time is running out for the Defenders. In a final desperate gambit, they quickly extend their trench network toward a perceived weak spot in the Invaders’ line in hopes of securing a breakthrough that will stave off defeat…for now.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: This scenario is suitable for 75- and 100-point armies.

name: Name
body:
As shown on the map, place three command trenches in each player’s Deployment Zone. Each player can place one bunker or guard tower anywhere within their Deployment Zone. Players then take turns each placing four additional trench terrain features in their Deployment Zones.
Players then take turns each placing three additional terrain features anywhere in their own Deployment Zones or in No Man’s Land. A terrain feature cannot be placed within 4" of another terrain feature, including a trench.
Players roll to determine who will deploy first and take the first turn. The winner takes the first turn and will deploy the first model/unit. Players take turns with each player deploying one model/unit to their Deployment Zone before their opponent places their next model/unit.

name: Name
body:
No Man’s Land: The entire area of No Man’s Land is rough terrain.
Hoard Revenant Mission: Players who include the Hoard Revenant in their force can undertake the following missions:
Defender: Hallowed Ground —The Hoard Revenant can make a Hallowed Ground special action once per game while completely within a trench in the Invader’s Deployment Zone. When he does so, all Invader upkeep spells within 10" of him expire and the Defender gains 1 additional War Chest point for this scenario. This action can only be taken once per game.
Invader: Hell on Earth—The Hoard Revenant can make the Gather Intel special action once per game while completely within a trench in the Defender’s Deployment Zone. When he does so, all Defender models within 10" of him lose Tough for one round, cannot have damage removed from them for one round, and the Invader receives 1 additional War Chest point for this scenario. This action can only be taken once per game.

name: Name
body: A player scores 2 Victory Points at the start of each of their turns for each of their opponent’s command trenches they are holding.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: Starting on the third round, a player securing all three of their opponent’s command trenches at the start of their turn wins the match and receives 6 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader model in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.
